D010-D006_h001.question:
It all started about seven months ago, a few months after my last relationship ended. For about two months, I was on top of the world. I barely slept but felt like I had endless energy, bouncing off the walls, feeling so euphoric. Ideas for new marketing campaigns just poured out of me, and I couldn't stop talking about them; it was like my mouth couldn't keep up with my thoughts. I even made some pretty significant investments in a few crypto projects – felt like a genius at the time, though now I'm seeing it was a bit reckless. I also found myself getting incredibly flirtatious, almost aggressively so, which isn't like me. I even had this unshakable feeling that my ex was secretly still seeing other people, even though we had broken up and there was no reason to think that. I’d also see fleeting figures out of the corner of my eye, just shadows really, but they’d make me jump.

Then, for the past five months, it’s been the complete opposite. This overwhelming sadness just draped over me, and nothing brings me joy anymore. Things that used to excite me about my job now just feel draining, and I can barely drag myself to work. Making even the simplest decisions, like what to wear, feels impossible. The worst part is, even with this dark cloud hanging over me, for about three weeks there, the visual disturbances continued, and this irrational belief that my ex was cheating on me persisted, even though my elevated mood had completely vanished. It’s like those thoughts and images have a life of their own, independent of how I’m feeling emotionally.
D010-D006_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D010-D006_h002.question:
Lately, I just haven't been myself. For about two months, I was bouncing off the walls. I barely slept, always buzzing with energy, and my patience was razor-thin. My poor husband, he’d just ask a simple question, and I’d snap at him. I was calling everyone I knew, sometimes in the middle of the night, feeling incredibly social and chatty, just wanting to connect. I even invested a chunk of our savings in some online venture that promised huge returns, barely looking at the details. I really thought it was going to make us rich.

Then, everything crashed quite abruptly, and for the past five months, I’ve felt utterly hollow. It’s a constant sadness, a heavy cloud that just won’t lift. I’ve been avoiding my census work and practically everyone. My mind feels so foggy, like I’m walking through a daze all the time. On top of all this, there are these strange things happening. Even when I’m not feeling high as a kite or deep in this depressive slump, I sometimes get this awful, metallic taste in my mouth, and I’m convinced my kidneys are shriveling up inside me, even though the doctors say I’m perfectly healthy. It happened for a couple of weeks after that manic spell, before this deep sadness really set in. Both the mania and the depression have really messed up my ability to do anything, but the doctors told me that my 'up' spells account for most of what's been going on all together.
D010-D006_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D010-D006_h003.question:
I'm not sure where to start, doctor. Everything just feels... off. For the past couple of months, I've been so on edge. Even the smallest thing, like a bug in my code, sets me off, and I just snap. There's this constant buzzing energy in me; I can't sit still, I’m always pacing or fiddling with my hands. My thoughts race, and sometimes I feel like I'm talking so fast, I can barely keep up with myself, and I can tell others have trouble understanding. It’s also led me to make some really dumb decisions, like pouring all my savings into a crypto coin that probably won’t even exist next year.

During that time, I also started feeling really strange things. I’d be sitting at my desk, and I could swear I felt insects crawling all over my skin, even when there was nothing there. And this conviction grew that my brain was slowly rotting, that my neural pathways were disintegrating. It got so bad that for about three weeks, these sensations and beliefs were still there even when the intense mood stuff seemed to calm down a bit, and I just felt utterly hollow and tearful. It’s been about five months of that empty feeling now, like I can’t enjoy anything, even my favorite games or coding. My mind feels so cloudy, like I’m constantly walking through a fog. This whole thing has really messed up my work; I’m barely keeping up.
D010-D006_h003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D010-D006_h004.question:
